name: Contemporary Magazine
tagline: Human rights reporting, art-directed like a monthly magazine.
idea: The site reads like a well-designed monthly magazine. Each edition opens with a cover story set as a two-page spread, then a contents grid of mixed tile sizes, colour-blocked report spreads and short field notes, so research feels inviting.
fit: Daybreak needs credible research to feel inviting. The edition structure gives features, reports and updates their own scale and colour, and places donate and newsletter asks where engaged readers arrive.
informedBy: A strong lead story with asymmetric layout instead of rows of equal cards
Report covers that stand apart from news
A serif reading face and captioned images
distinct: The only concept built from colour-block spreads and a mosaic contents grid, with oversized italic headlines, tilted report covers and circular, offset image crops.
buttons: Pill buttons: tomato for Donate, ink for main actions, outlined for downloads; arrow links; soft tags.
imageDirection: Natural colour, cropped like a collage: tall and wide crops, circular cut-outs and offset colour-block frames, with captions.
navigation: Centred wordmark with edition date, dotted section row and a tomato Donate pill.
visualCharacter: Colourful, art-directed, editorial; big italic serif headlines.
contentEmphasis: Features and stories first, with reports as collectable objects.
bestFor: Reaching new and younger supporters through storytelling while keeping research credible and easy to browse.
tradeoffs: Needs strong images and editorial effort for every edition; bright colour may feel less formal for policy audiences; display type needs care.
